newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Fernandez waves Argentine labor law decree threat.
newsitem.headline: Fernandez waves Argentine labor law decree threat.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Friday he would advise President Carlos Menem to introduce labor law reforms by decree if unions and Congress try to alter the current reform project.
"The decrees were suspended for the sake of consensus. But if it is not respected I would advise Menem to go back to the decrees," Fernandez told reporters.
The Peronist president's attempts to modernize Argentina's labor legislation by decree met stiff union opposition and were blocked by the courts at the beginning of the year.

Arguing it was the best way to fight unemployment now standing at 16.1 pecent, Menem proposed decentralizing pay talks away from union control and swapping redundancy payouts for unemployment insurance. He also wanted to throw open union controlled health care schemes to free competition.

After three-way talks between the government, industry bosses and unions proved fruitless, Menem struck a deal with the traditionally pro-Peronist CGT union federation for a watered-down version of the reforms, now in Congress.
Opposition trade unions staged a national strike against the labor reforms Thursday, but the CGT, the largest labor movement, opposed the strike.

Fernandez said he would advise Menem to withdraw the "Act of Coincidence" with the CGT now being processed in Congress, if there is pressure from the CGT and "some Peronist senators" to water down the reforms further, and reform by decree.
"In those decrees I would also recommend opening up the health care schemes to private competition and eliminating the rigidities in labor legislation," said Fernandez.
